thread.title: Apple’s stock gets blame for a quarter of the Dow’s 200-point skid early Monday

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Apple’s stock gets blame for a quarter of the Dow’s 200-point skid early Monday
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average
 DJIA, -1.77%
 was trading solidly lower early Monday, with shares of Apple Inc.
 AAPL, -4.23%
 producing the greatest headwind for the price-weighted benchmark in early action. Shares of Apple were down more than $8.15, or 4.1%, which equates to a 55-point loss for the Dow. Apple’s stock was tumbling after Lumentum Holdings Inc.
 LITE, -30.63%
 slashed its earnings and revenue outlook, saying it received a request from “one of its largest industrial and consumer customers for laser diodes for 3D sensing” to “materially reduce shipments” during the fiscal second quarter, which ends in December. A separate report from JPMorgan Chase & Co. analysts was negative on the iPhone maker. That customer is believed to be Apple . The Dow was down 235 points, or 0.9%, at 25,752. A $1 move in any one of the Dow’s components translates to a a roughly 6.8-point swing. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 index
 SPX, -1.44%
 fell 0.9% at 2,756 and the Nasdaq Composite Index
 COMP, -2.25%
 was trading 1.5% lower at 7,292. Apple is the biggest company by market value and one of the most influential within the Dow by virtue of its share price. That fact makes Apple a key catalyst for market moves among the three main stock benchmarks.
